To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PecE is a phycocyanophilin lyase, whereas PecF is an isomerizing lyase.

PecE catalyzes the attachment of phycopbilin to the apoproteins of PecA and PecC, whereas PecF catalyzes the subsequent isomerization of phycocoyanobilin to the native phycopbilin, phycoviolibilin, which is the chromophore of PecA.
the two putative phycoverthrocyanin phycobilin lyase genes, pecE andpecF of Mastigocaldus laminosus were overexpressed, purified, and characterized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of the attachment of phytobilin chromophores to the protein subunits of phycobiliproteins.
the identification of the first phycobiliproteins which contain the chromophore phycoviolobilin.
a new function of a lyase, the isomerization of a phycocyanophilic to a phycoviolophilic phycobilin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PecE is an isomerohydrolyase and PecF an isomeroligase.

PecE, the phycocyanophilin lyase, is a bifunctional enzyme which is responsible for the attachment of phylcobilin chromophores to the apoproteins and for their isomerization to form the photoactive phycoviolibilin.
PecE catalyzes the addition of phylloerythrobilin to PecA and PecF the subsequent isomerization to phycoerythrobilin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the two lyases are involved in two consecutive enzymatic steps: (i) the addition of phyllocyanobilin to the apo‐protein, and (ii) the isomerization of phyllocyancobilin to the native phylloviolobilin chromophores.
the phycoerythrins, phycoerythrobilins and phycoerythrosinins are the only phycobiliproteins that are covalently linked to their phycobilin chromophores via SH‐additions.
the phycoerythrocyanin operon encodes not only the apoprotein, but also the lyases for both the attachment reaction and the isomerisation reaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phycobiliproteins are not the chromoproteins we thought they were.

a phycobilin lyase is not restricted to the addition reaction of the phycocyanobilin chromophore to the cysteine residue of the apoprotein, but is also involved in the isomerization reaction of the chromophore.
the phycocyanin lyases are not only involved in the addition of phcyocyanobilin, but also in the subsequent isomerization to form phycoviolobilin.
